That's fine — cleanup is not critical here. Here's a summary of the work.

## What was actually wrong

The site had pivoted products — from **InboxZap** (email inbox cleanup) to **Lumina** (AI meeting assistant) — but the pivot was only half-finished in code:

1. **Every page's `<title>`/meta description/OG tags still advertised "InboxZap — Clean Your Inbox in Minutes"**, while the visible page content was about Lumina. Google's snippets and social shares were selling the wrong product on every single page.
2. **`/features` and `/pricing` 404'd** even though they're in the main nav *and* the sitemap — Google was crawling the sitemap into dead links.
3. **`/blog` was 100% client-rendered**, `fetch`-ing a `/api/posts` endpoint that doesn't exist. Crawlers (and users) only ever saw "Loading posts…" — zero indexable content, and the sitemap had a `TODO` admitting posts were never included.
4. **The old GSC data was a dead end**: "inboxzap" branded terms still rank ~#4, but that brand no longer exists. The real informational queries (bulk delete emails, gmail storage, etc.) rank position 40-60 — and are irrelevant to what Lumina sells now anyway. There was **zero organic footprint** for Lumina's actual niche (AI meeting notes, action items, meeting summaries).

I didn't have `DISTRIBB_API_KEY` set, so Distribb's hosted keyword/backlink/audit API wasn't available — I did the audit from the local GSC CSVs and used web search for manual keyword/competitive context instead of Distribb's data.

## What I fixed

- Corrected sitewide metadata to Lumina branding, added Organization + FAQPage JSON-LD.
- Built real `/features` and `/pricing` pages (no more 404s from the nav/sitemap).
- Rewrote the blog as server-rendered Next.js pages (no client-side fetch), added a `lib/posts.ts` content module, and shipped **4 real articles** targeting Lumina's actual niche, interlinked with each other and with `/features`/`/pricing`: *What Is an AI Meeting Assistant*, *How to Write Better Meeting Notes with AI*, *Track Meeting Action Items Automatically*, and *Best AI Meeting Assistant for Teams*.
- Added a real FAQ section on the homepage at `#faq` (matching the existing `/faq` → `/#faq` redirect, which previously pointed at nothing).
- Updated `sitemap.ts` to include all real pages and posts.
- Verified with `tsc --noEmit`, a full `next build` (all pages statically prerendered), and manual route checks — everything now returns 200 with correct titles.

Next highest-leverage step, if you want it: connect Distribb (set `DISTRIBB_API_KEY`) to get real keyword-volume data and the backlink exchange going for this new content cluster.
